title: Persecution scatters the church; Philip in Samaria; Simon Magus + the Ethiopian eunuch baptized

paragraphs.text: And Saul was consenting unto his death. And there arose on that day a great persecution against the church which was in Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judaea and Samaria, except the apostles.
paragraphs.original: Σαῦλος δὲ ἦν συνευδοκῶν τῇ ἀναιρέσει αὐτοῦ. Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ διωγμὸς μέγας ἐπὶ τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τὴν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις· πάντες δὲ διεσπάρησαν κατὰ τὰς χώρας τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Σαμαρείας πλὴν τῶν ἀποστόλων.
paragraphs.translit: Saulos de ēn syneudokōn tē anairesei autou. Egeneto de en ekeinē tē hēmera diōgmos megas epi tēn ekklēsian tēn en Hierosolymois· pantes de diesparēsan kata tas chōras tēs Ioudaias kai Samareias plēn tōn apostolōn.

paragraphs.text: And devout men buried Stephen, and made great lamentation over him.
paragraphs.original: συνεκόμισαν δὲ τὸν Στέφανον ἄνδρες εὐλαβεῖς καὶ ἐποίησαν κοπετὸν μέγαν ἐπʼ αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: synekomisan de ton Stephanon andres eulabeis kai epoiēsan kopeton megan epʼ autō.

paragraphs.text: But Saul laid waste the church, entering into every house, and dragging men and women committed them to prison.
paragraphs.original: Σαῦλος δὲ ἐλυμαίνετο τὴν ἐκκλησίαν κατὰ τοὺς οἴκους εἰσπορευόμενος, σύρων τε ἄνδρας καὶ γυναῖκας παρεδίδου εἰς φυλακήν.
paragraphs.translit: Saulos de elymaineto tēn ekklēsian kata tous oikous eisporeuomenos, syrōn te andras kai gynaikas paredidou eis phylakēn.

paragraphs.text: They therefore that were scattered abroad, went about preaching the word.
paragraphs.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διασπαρέντες διῆλθον εὐαγγελιζόμενοι τὸν λόγον.
paragraphs.translit: Hoi men oun diasparentes diēlthon euangelizomenoi ton logon.

paragraphs.text: And Philip went down to the city of Samaria, and proclaimed unto them the Christ.
paragraphs.original: Φίλιππος δὲ κατελθὼν εἰς τὴν πόλιν τῆς Σαμαρείας ἐκήρυσσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν χριστόν.
paragraphs.translit: Philippos de katelthōn eis tēn polin tēs Samareias ekēryssen autois ton christon.

paragraphs.text: And the multitudes gave heed with one accord unto the things that were spoken by Philip, when they heard, and saw the signs which he did.
paragraphs.original: προσεῖχον δὲ οἱ ὄχλοι τοῖς λεγομένοις ὑπὸ τοῦ Φιλίππου ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐν τῷ ἀκούειν αὐτοὺς καὶ βλέπειν τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐποίει·
paragraphs.translit: proseichon de hoi ochloi tois legomenois hypo tou Philippou homothymadon en tō akouein autous kai blepein ta sēmeia ha epoiei·

paragraphs.text: For [from] many of those that had unclean spirits, they came out, crying with a loud voice: and many that were palsied, and that were lame, were healed.
paragraphs.original: πολλοὶ γὰρ τῶν ἐχόντων πνεύματα ἀκάθαρτα βοῶντα φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἐξήρχοντο, πολλοὶ δὲ παραλελυμένοι καὶ χωλοὶ ἐθεραπεύθησαν·
paragraphs.translit: polloi gar tōn echontōn pneumata akatharta boōnta phōnē megalē exērchonto, polloi de paralelymenoi kai chōloi etherapeuthēsan·

paragraphs.text: And there was much joy in that city.
paragraphs.original: ἐγένετο δὲ πολλὴ χαρὰ ἐν τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ.
paragraphs.translit: egeneto de pollē chara en tē polei ekeinē.

paragraphs.text: But there was a certain man, Simon by name, who beforetime in the city used sorcery, and amazed the people of Samaria, giving out that himself was some great one:
paragraphs.original: Ἀνὴρ δέ τις ὀνόματι Σίμων προϋπῆρχεν ἐν τῇ πόλει μαγεύων καὶ ἐξιστάνων τὸ ἔθνος τῆς Σαμαρείας, λέγων εἶναί τινα ἑαυτὸν μέγαν,
paragraphs.translit: Anēr de tis onomati Simōn proupērchen en tē polei mageuōn kai existanōn to ethnos tēs Samareias, legōn einai tina heauton megan,

paragraphs.text: to whom they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is that power of God which is called Great.
paragraphs.original: ᾧ προσεῖχον πάντες ἀπὸ μικροῦ ἕως μεγάλου λέγοντες· Οὗτός ἐστιν ἡ Δύναμις τοῦ θεοῦ ἡ καλουμένη Μεγάλη.
paragraphs.translit: hō proseichon pantes apo mikrou heōs megalou legontes· Houtos estin hē Dynamis tou theou hē kaloumenē Megalē.

paragraphs.text: And they gave heed to him, because that of long time he had amazed them with his sorceries.
paragraphs.original: προσεῖχον δὲ αὐτῷ διὰ τὸ ἱκανῷ χρόνῳ ταῖς μαγείαις ἐξεστακέναι αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: proseichon de autō dia to hikanō chronō tais mageiais exestakenai autous.

paragraphs.text: But when they believed Philip preaching good tidings concerning the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.
paragraphs.original: ὅτε δὲ ἐπίστευσαν τῷ Φιλίππῳ εὐαγγελιζομένῳ περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ ὀνόματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἐβαπτίζοντο ἄνδρες τε καὶ γυναῖκες.
paragraphs.translit: hote de episteusan tō Philippō euangelizomenō peri tēs basileias tou theou kai tou onomatos Iēsou Christou, ebaptizonto andres te kai gynaikes.

paragraphs.text: And Simon also himself believed: and being baptized, he continued with Philip; and beholding signs and great miracles wrought, he was amazed.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Σίμων καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπίστευσεν, καὶ βαπτισθεὶς ἦν προσκαρτερῶν τῷ Φιλίππῳ, θεωρῶν τε σημεῖα καὶ δυνάμεις μεγάλας γινομένας ἐξίστατο.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Simōn kai autos episteusen, kai baptistheis ēn proskarterōn tō Philippō, theōrōn te sēmeia kai dynameis megalas ginomenas existato.

paragraphs.text: Now when the apostles that were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John:
paragraphs.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἀπόστολοι ὅτι δέδεκται ἡ Σαμάρεια τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀπέστειλαν πρὸς αὐτοὺς Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην,
paragraphs.translit: Akousantes de hoi en Hierosolymois apostoloi hoti dedektai hē Samareia ton logon tou theou, apesteilan pros autous Petron kai Iōannēn,

paragraphs.text: who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Spirit:
paragraphs.original: οἵτινες καταβάντες προσηύξαντο περὶ αὐτῶν ὅπως λάβωσιν πνεῦμα ἅγιον·
paragraphs.translit: hoitines katabantes prosēuxanto peri autōn hopōs labōsin pneuma hagion·

paragraphs.text: for as yet it was fallen upon none of them: only they had been baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
paragraphs.original: οὐδέπω γὰρ ἦν ἐπʼ οὐδενὶ αὐτῶν ἐπιπεπτωκός, μόνον δὲ βεβαπτισμένοι ὑπῆρχον εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: oudepō gar ēn epʼ oudeni autōn epipeptōkos, monon de bebaptismenoi hypērchon eis to onoma tou kyriou Iēsou.

paragraphs.text: Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
paragraphs.original: τότε ἐπετίθεσαν τὰς χεῖρας ἐπʼ αὐτούς, καὶ ἐλάμβανον πνεῦμα ἅγιον.
paragraphs.translit: tote epetithesan tas cheiras epʼ autous, kai elambanon pneuma hagion.

paragraphs.text: Now when Simon saw that through the laying on of the apostles` hands the Holy Spirit was given, he offered them money,
paragraphs.original: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Σίμων ὅτι διὰ τῆς ἐπιθέσεως τῶν χειρῶν τῶν ἀποστόλων δίδοται τὸ πνεῦμα προσήνεγκεν αὐτοῖς χρήματα
paragraphs.translit: idōn de ho Simōn hoti dia tēs epitheseōs tōn cheirōn tōn apostolōn didotai to pneuma prosēnenken autois chrēmata

paragraphs.text: saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay my hands, he may receive the Holy Spirit.
paragraphs.original: λέγων· Δότε κἀμοὶ τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην ἵνα ᾧ ἐὰν ἐπιθῶ τὰς χεῖρας λαμβάνῃ πνεῦμα ἅγιον.
paragraphs.translit: legōn· Dote kamoi tēn exousian tautēn hina hō ean epithō tas cheiras lambanē pneuma hagion.

paragraphs.text: But Peter said unto him, Thy silver perish with thee, because thou hast thought to obtain the gift of God with money.
paragraphs.original: Πέτρος δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Τὸ ἀργύριόν σου σὺν σοὶ εἴη εἰς ἀπώλειαν ὅτι τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐνόμισας διὰ χρημάτων κτᾶσθαι.
paragraphs.translit: Petros de eipen pros auton· To argyrion sou syn soi eiē eis apōleian hoti tēn dōrean tou theou enomisas dia chrēmatōn ktasthai.

paragraphs.text: Thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter: for thy heart is not right before God.
paragraphs.original: οὐκ ἔστιν σοι μερὶς οὐδὲ κλῆρος ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ, ἡ γὰρ καρδία σου οὐκ ἔστιν εὐθεῖα ἔναντι τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ouk estin soi meris oude klēros en tō logō toutō, hē gar kardia sou ouk estin eutheia enanti tou theou.

paragraphs.text: Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray the Lord, if perhaps the thought of thy heart shall be forgiven thee.
paragraphs.original: μετανόησον οὖν ἀπὸ τῆς κακίας σου ταύτης, καὶ δεήθητι τοῦ κυρίου εἰ ἄρα ἀφεθήσεταί σοι ἡ ἐπίνοια τῆς καρδίας σου·
paragraphs.translit: metanoēson oun apo tēs kakias sou tautēs, kai deēthēti tou kyriou ei ara aphethēsetai soi hē epinoia tēs kardias sou·

paragraphs.text: For I see that thou art in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity.
paragraphs.original: εἰς γὰρ χολὴν πικρίας καὶ σύνδεσμον ἀδικίας ὁρῶ σε ὄντα.
paragraphs.translit: eis gar cholēn pikrias kai syndesmon adikias horō se onta.

paragraphs.text: And Simon answered and said, Pray ye for me to the Lord, that none of the things which ye have spoken come upon me.
paragraphs.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Σίμων εἶπεν· Δεήθητε ὑμεῖς ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ πρὸς τὸν κύριον ὅπως μηδὲν ἐπέλθῃ ἐπʼ ἐμὲ ὧν εἰρήκατε.
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de ho Simōn eipen· Deēthēte hymeis hyper emou pros ton kyrion hopōs mēden epelthē epʼ eme hōn eirēkate.

paragraphs.text: They therefore, when they had testified and spoken the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem, and preached the gospel to many villages of the Samaritans.
paragraphs.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διαμαρτυράμενοι καὶ λαλήσαντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου ὑπέστρεφον εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, πολλάς τε κώμας τῶν Σαμαριτῶν εὐηγγελίζοντο.
paragraphs.translit: Hoi men oun diamartyramenoi kai lalēsantes ton logon tou kyriou hypestrephon eis Hierosolyma, pollas te kōmas tōn Samaritōn euēngelizonto.

paragraphs.text: But an angel of the Lord spake unto Philip, saying, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza: the same is desert.
paragraphs.original: Ἄγγελος δὲ κυρίου ἐλάλησεν πρὸς Φίλιππον λέγων· Ἀνάστηθι καὶ πορεύου κατὰ μεσημβρίαν ἐπὶ τὴν ὁδὸν τὴν καταβαίνουσαν ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλὴμ εἰς Γάζαν· αὕτη ἐστὶν ἔρημος.
paragraphs.translit: Angelos de kyriou elalēsen pros Philippon legōn· Anastēthi kai poreuou kata mesēmbrian epi tēn hodon tēn katabainousan apo Ierousalēm eis Gazan· hautē estin erēmos.

paragraphs.text: And he arose and went: and behold, a man of Ethiopia, a eunuch of great authority under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasure, who had come to Jerusalem to worship;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀναστὰς ἐπορεύθη, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ Αἰθίοψ εὐνοῦχος δυνάστης Κανδάκης βασιλίσσης Αἰθιόπων, ὃς ἦν ἐπὶ πάσης τῆς γάζης αὐτῆς, ὃς ἐληλύθει προσκυνήσων εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ,
paragraphs.translit: kai anastas eporeuthē, kai idou anēr Aithiops eunouchos dynastēs Kandakēs basilissēs Aithiopōn, hos ēn epi pasēs tēs gazēs autēs, hos elēlythei proskynēsōn eis Ierousalēm,

paragraphs.text: and he was returning and sitting in his chariot, and was reading the prophet Isaiah.
paragraphs.original: ἦν τε ὑποστρέφων καὶ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τοῦ ἅρματος αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀνεγίνωσκεν τὸν προφήτην Ἠσαΐαν.
paragraphs.translit: ēn te hypostrephōn kai kathēmenos epi tou harmatos autou kai aneginōsken ton prophētēn Ēsaian.

paragraphs.text: And the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα τῷ Φιλίππῳ· Πρόσελθε καὶ κολλήθητι τῷ ἅρματι τούτῳ.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de to pneuma tō Philippō· Proselthe kai kollēthēti tō harmati toutō.

paragraphs.text: And Philip ran to him, and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest?
paragraphs.original: προσδραμὼν δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος ἤκουσεν αὐτοῦ ἀναγινώσκοντος Ἠσαΐαν τὸν προφήτην καὶ εἶπεν· Ἆρά γε γινώσκεις ἃ ἀναγινώσκεις;
paragraphs.translit: prosdramōn de ho Philippos ēkousen autou anaginōskontos Ēsaian ton prophētēn kai eipen· Ara ge ginōskeis ha anaginōskeis;

paragraphs.text: And he said, How can I, except some one shall guide me? And he besought Philip to come up and sit with him.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Πῶς γὰρ ἂν δυναίμην ἐὰν μή τις ὁδηγήσει με; παρεκάλεσέν τε τὸν Φίλιππον ἀναβάντα καθίσαι σὺν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen· Pōs gar an dynaimēn ean mē tis hodēgēsei me; parekalesen te ton Philippon anabanta kathisai syn autō.

paragraphs.text: Now the passage of the Scripture which he was reading was this, He was led as a sheep to the slaughter; And as a lamb before his shearer is dumb, So he openeth not his mouth:
paragraphs.original: ἡ δὲ περιοχὴ τῆς γραφῆς ἣν ἀνεγίνωσκεν ἦν αὕτη· Ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη, καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ κείραντος αὐτὸν ἄφωνος, οὕτως οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hē de periochē tēs graphēs hēn aneginōsken ēn hautē· Hōs probaton epi sphagēn ēchthē, kai hōs amnos enantion tou keirantos auton aphōnos, houtōs ouk anoigei to stoma autou.

paragraphs.text: In his humiliation his judgment was taken away: His generation who shall declare? For his life is taken from the earth.
paragraphs.original: ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει ἡ κρίσις αὐτοῦ ἤρθη· τὴν γενεὰν αὐτοῦ τίς διηγήσεται; ὅτι αἴρεται ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: en tē tapeinōsei hē krisis autou ērthē· tēn genean autou tis diēgēsetai; hoti airetai apo tēs gēs hē zōē autou.

paragraphs.text: And the eunuch answered Philip, and said, I pray thee, of whom speaketh the prophet this? of himself, or of some other?
paragraphs.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ εὐνοῦχος τῷ Φιλίππῳ εἶπεν· Δέομαί σου, περὶ τίνος ὁ προφήτης λέγει τοῦτο; περὶ ἑαυτοῦ ἢ περὶ ἑτέρου τινός;
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de ho eunouchos tō Philippō eipen· Deomai sou, peri tinos ho prophētēs legei touto; peri heautou ē peri heterou tinos;

paragraphs.text: And Philip opened his mouth, and beginning from this Scripture, preached unto him Jesus.
paragraphs.original: ἀνοίξας δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς γραφῆς ταύτης εὐηγγελίσατο αὐτῷ τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
paragraphs.translit: anoixas de ho Philippos to stoma autou kai arxamenos apo tēs graphēs tautēs euēngelisato autō ton Iēsoun.

paragraphs.text: And as they went on the way, they came unto a certain water; and the eunuch saith, Behold, [here is] water; what doth hinder me to be baptized?
paragraphs.original: ὡς δὲ ἐπορεύοντο κατὰ τὴν ὁδόν, ἦλθον ἐπί τι ὕδωρ, καί φησιν ὁ εὐνοῦχος· Ἰδοὺ ὕδωρ, τί κωλύει με βαπτισθῆναι;
paragraphs.translit: hōs de eporeuonto kata tēn hodon, ēlthon epi ti hydōr, kai phēsin ho eunouchos· Idou hydōr, ti kōlyei me baptisthēnai;

paragraphs.text: [And Philip said, If thou believest with all thy heart, thou mayest. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.]
And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they both went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐκέλευσεν στῆναι τὸ ἅρμα, καὶ κατέβησαν ἀμφότεροι εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ ὅ τε Φίλιππος καὶ ὁ εὐνοῦχος, καὶ ἐβάπτισεν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ekeleusen stēnai to harma, kai katebēsan amphoteroi eis to hydōr ho te Philippos kai ho eunouchos, kai ebaptisen auton.

paragraphs.text: And when they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip; and the eunuch saw him no more, for he went on his way rejoicing.
paragraphs.original: ὅτε δὲ ἀνέβησαν ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος, πνεῦμα κυρίου ἥρπασεν τὸν Φίλιππον, καὶ οὐκ εἶδεν αὐτὸν οὐκέτι ὁ εὐνοῦχος, ἐπορεύετο γὰρ τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ χαίρων.
paragraphs.translit: hote de anebēsan ek tou hydatos, pneuma kyriou hērpasen ton Philippon, kai ouk eiden auton ouketi ho eunouchos, eporeueto gar tēn hodon autou chairōn.

paragraphs.text: But Philip was found at Azotus: and passing through he preached the gospel to all the cities, till he came to Caesarea.
paragraphs.original: Φίλιππος δὲ εὑρέθη εἰς Ἄζωτον, καὶ διερχόμενος εὐηγγελίζετο τὰς πόλεις πάσας ἕως τοῦ ἐλθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς Καισάρειαν.
paragraphs.translit: Philippos de heurethē eis Azōton, kai dierchomenos euēngelizeto tas poleis pasas heōs tou elthein auton eis Kaisareian.
